passage: In the school counsellor's small room, with its box of tissues and poster of a mountain, Tenzin and his mother Binita sat side by side for the third time. This week they had brought a sheet of paper. On it, in Tenzin's handwriting: Weekends, home by 9:30. Text when I reach, text when I leave. If plans change, call, don't text. Review in four weeks. Binita had added one line of her own: I will not call more than once unless he misses a check-in. The counsellor read it out. "Four weeks from today, then." Tenzin grinned. "If I'm on time every week, can it be ten o'clock?" Binita smiled too. "Show me first."

qa.q: By what time must Tenzin be home on weekends?
qa.a: He must be home by 9:30 on weekends.

qa.q: What does Tenzin's grin and question about ten o'clock suggest?
qa.a: He feels hopeful and motivated, understanding that being reliable can earn him more freedom.

qa.q: What makes this agreement likely to work?
qa.a: It has a clear curfew, a contact plan, a review date and a limit on Binita's calls, so both sides know the rules and can build trust step by step.

qa.q: What is Binita learning in this arrangement?
qa.a: She is learning to keep a boundary while letting Tenzin practise freedom, trusting him more as he proves reliable.

grounding: It shows a parent and teen agreeing on a curfew, contact plan and review date, with reliability earning more freedom and the parent learning to let him practise.

passage:
Hi Pradeep Mama,
You asked how things are with Papa after all the fights. Honestly? Better. Last Sunday we sat down and made actual rules. I can go out with friends on Fridays, home by ten. I text when I reach and when I leave. If I'm going to be late, I call before, not after. And we'll look at it again after a month.
The funny thing is, Papa also had to agree to stuff. He won't call me ten times, only if I miss a text. Last Friday I was home at 9:50 and he just said, "Good," and went back to his newspaper. 🙂
If I keep this up, he said we can talk about Saturday nights too.
Siddharth

qa.q: How often will Papa call Siddharth now?
qa.a: He won't call ten times; he will only call if Siddharth misses a text.

qa.q: How does Siddharth feel about the new rules?
qa.a: Siddharth feels hopeful and a bit proud, seeing that keeping the rules is already earning trust and maybe more freedom.

qa.q: Why is the one-month review a smart part of the plan?
qa.a: It gives both of them a set time to see how it went, so trust can grow step by step instead of through fights.

qa.q: How might Papa have felt when Siddharth came home at 9:50?
qa.a: He probably felt relieved and pleased that the plan was working, which is why he just said "Good."

grounding: It illustrates a teen and parent agreeing on a curfew, a contact plan and a review, so reliability earns freedom while the parent holds a boundary and lets go a little.
